'''Lucas Vázquez Iglesias''' (born 1 July 1991) is a Spanish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[right-back]] or [[Winger (association football)|winger]] for {{German football updater|BaLeverk}} club [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]].

Starting his career at [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], Vázquez made his first-team debut in 2015 after a season on loan at [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]]. He made his [[La Liga]] debut with the latter. Since returning to Real Madrid in 2015 he has appeared in more than 400 matches for the club in all competitions and has won 23 major trophies including five [[UEFA Champions League|Champions Leagues]] and four [[La Liga]] titles. After leaving Real Madrid as a free agent in summer 2025, Vázquez moved to Bundesliga's Bayer Leverkusen.

Vázquez represented [[Spain national football team|Spain]] at [[UEFA Euro 2016|Euro 2016]] and the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018 World Cup]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Curtis, Spain|Curtis]], Galicia, Vázquez arrived at [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]'s youth system in 2007, aged 16.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lucas Vazquez Iglesias |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/football/first-team/players/lucas-vazquez-iglesias |access-date=2025-02-07 |website=www.realmadrid.com}}</ref> He made his senior debut in the [[2010–11 Segunda División B|2010–11 season]] with the [[Real Madrid C|C-team]]. He scored four goals in 23 games in [[2011–12 Segunda División B|the following season]] to help the [[Real Madrid Castilla|reserves]] return to the [[Segunda División]] after a five-year absence. His first goal came on 25 February 2012 in a 2–2 home draw against [[La Roda CF|La Roda]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/ActualidadCantera1112/1330087479318/noticia/Noticia/Fourteen_players_score_for_Castilla.htm|title=Fourteen players score for Castilla|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=27 February 2012|access-date=24 May 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130201013136/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/ActualidadCantera1112/1330087479318/noticia/Noticia/Fourteen_players_score_for_Castilla.htm|archive-date=1 February 2013}}</ref>

Vázquez made his first appearance in the second level on 17 August 2012, playing six minutes in a 1–2 away loss against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2012/08/17/futbol/2adivision/1345237033.html|title=Cavenaghi toma los mandos del 'Submarino'|trans-title=Cavenaghi takes charge of the 'Submarine'|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|first=Diego|last=Acedo|language=es|date=17 August 2012|access-date=24 May 2013}}</ref> He scored his first professional goal on 15 October, netting the winner in a 3–2 home success over [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2012/10/15/futbol/2adivision/1350334344.html|title=El 'loco' Castilla enajena a Las Palmas|trans-title='Crazy' Castilla estrange Las Palmas|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=15 October 2012|access-date=20 August 2014}}</ref>

====Loan to Espanyol====
On 19 August 2014, Vázquez was loaned to [[La Liga]]'s [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], in a [[2014–15 La Liga|season]]-long deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://rcdespanyol.com/principal.php?modulo=detalleNoticia&idnoticia=18263&idseccion=28&idlinkchk=0&idmenu=9&idsubmenu=108|title=Lucas Vázquez jugarà cedit a l'Espanyol|trans-title=Lucas Vázquez will play on loan at Espanyol|publisher=RCD Espanyol|language=ca|date=19 August 2014|access-date=20 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140820193500/http://rcdespanyol.com/principal.php?modulo=detalleNoticia&idnoticia=18263&idseccion=28&idlinkchk=0&idmenu=9&idsubmenu=108|archive-date=20 August 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his debut in the competition on 30 August, coming on as a second-half [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Salva Sevilla]] in a 1–2 home loss against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2014_15/primera/jornada_2/esp_sev/|title=El Sevilla impone su oficio ante el Espanyol|trans-title=Sevilla lay down the law against Espanyol|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=31 August 2014|access-date=3 June 2015}}</ref> 

Vázquez scored his first goal in the [[Spanish football league system|Spanish top flight]] on 5 October 2014, netting the first in a 2–0 home success over [[Real Sociedad]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2014_15/primera/jornada_7/esp_rso/|title=El Espanyol pone a Arrasate contra las cuerdas|trans-title=Espanyol put Arrasate against the wall|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=5 October 2014|access-date=3 June 2015}}</ref> On 3 June of the following year, he signed a four-year permanent deal with the ''Pericos'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://rcdespanyol.com/principal.php?modulo=detalleNoticia&idnoticia=20044&idmenu=9|title=Lucas Vázquez, perico|trans-title=Lucas Vázquez, a parakeet|publisher=RCD Espanyol|language=ca|date=3 June 2015|access-date=3 June 2015|archive-date=11 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150611122235/http://www.rcdespanyol.com/principal.php?modulo=detalleNoticia&idnoticia=20044&idmenu=9|url-status=dead}}</ref> for a [[Euro|€]]2&nbsp;million fee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fichajes.net/noticias/espanyol-comprara-lucas-vazquez-20150529.html|title=El Espanyol comprará a Lucas Vázquez|trans-title=Espanyol will buy Lucas Vázquez|publisher=Fichajes|language=es|date=29 May 2015|access-date=3 June 2015}}</ref>

===Return to Real Madrid===
[[File:Lucas Vazquez.JPG|thumb|Vázquez playing for [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 2016|left|426x426px]]
On 30 June 2015, Real Madrid exercised their buyback clause and Vázquez returned to the club.<ref>{{cite web |date=2 July 2015 |title=Official announcement: Lucas Vázquez |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/07/official-announcement-lucas-vazquez |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924144246/http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/07/official-announcement-lucas-vazquez |archive-date=24 September 2015 |access-date=2 July 2015 |publisher=Real Madrid CF}}</ref> He made his debut on 12 September in a 6–0 away win over his former team Espanyol,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laliga.es/noticias/un-historico-ronaldo-lidera-la-goleada-al-espanyol|title=Un histórico Ronaldo lidera la goleada al Espanyol|trans-title=Historical Ronaldo leads routing of Espanyol|publisher=[[La Liga]]|language=es|date=12 September 2015|access-date=12 September 2015}}</ref> and his first start came a week later, in a 1–0 home defeat of [[Granada CF|Granada]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laliga.es/noticias/el-real-madrid-se-impone-al-granada-por-la-minima|title=El Real Madrid se impone al Granada por la mínima|trans-title=Real Madrid defeat Granada by the odd goal|publisher=La Liga|language=es|date=19 September 2015|access-date=19 September 2015}}</ref>

Vázquez scored his first competitive goal on 30 December 2015, replacing [[Karim Benzema]] for the final 15 minutes of the league fixture against Real Sociedad and netting in a 3–1 success at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/35155089|title=Real Madrid 3–1 Real Sociedad|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=30 December 2015|access-date=30 December 2015}}</ref> He contributed with seven appearances in [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League|the season]]'s [[UEFA Champions League]], as the tournament ended in a win; in [[2016 UEFA Champions League final|the final]] against [[Atlético Madrid]], he again came on for the Frenchman late into the second half of a 1–1 draw, and converted his attempt in the [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]] triumph.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/022d-0e957c5979eb-37493cb53cd0-1000--spot-on-real-madrid-defeat-atletico-in-final-again/|title=Spot-on Real Madrid defeat Atlético in final again|publisher=UEFA|date=28 May 2016|access-date=29 May 2016}}</ref>

Vázquez started the [[2016 UEFA Super Cup]] against fellow Spaniards Sevilla, providing an assist to [[Sergio Ramos]] in injury time to take the game to [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]], where Real Madrid eventually won 3–2.<ref>{{Cite web |last=UEFA.com |date=9 August 2016 |title=Carvajal wonder goal wins Super Cup for Madrid |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefasupercup/news/0250-0c5111919148-7ee9946e9786-1000--carvajal-wonder-goal-wins-super-cup-for-madrid/ |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=UEFA.com |language=en}}</ref> He signed a new contract on 26 October 2016, running until 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 October 2016 |title=Official Announcement: Lucas Vázquez {{!}} Real Madrid CF |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2016/10/official-statement-lucas-vazquez |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161029043152/http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2016/10/official-statement-lucas-vazquez |archive-date=2016-10-29 |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=Real Madrid C.F. - Web Oficial |language=en}}</ref> 

Vázquez appeared 33 times during [[2016–17 La Liga|2016–17]] and scored twice,<ref>{{Cite news |title=Osasuna 1-3 Real Madrid: Cristiano Ronaldo, Isco and  Lucas Vasquez help Real battle past Osasuna |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/osasuna-vs-r-madrid/362908 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241130063808/https://www.skysports.com/football/osasuna-vs-r-madrid/362908 |archive-date=2024-11-30 |access-date=2026-08-12 |work=Sky Sports |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=26 April 2017 |title=Deportivo La Coruna 2–6 Real Madrid PLAYER RATINGS as Isco dazed hosts in stunning performance |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/match-reports/real-madrid-player-ratings-deportivo-10303769 |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=[[Daily Mirror]]}}</ref> helping Real Madrid to its first league in five years.<ref>{{Cite news |title=El Real Madrid, campeón de LaLiga Santander 2016/17 |trans-title=Real Madrid, LaLiga Santander champions 2016/17 |url=http://www.laliga.es/noticias/real-madrid-campeon-de-laliga-santander-2016-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190712180825/http://www.laliga.es/noticias/real-madrid-campeon-de-laliga-santander-2016-17 |archive-date=2019-07-12 |access-date=2026-08-12 |work=Liga de Fútbol Profesional |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2017-05-20 |title=Malaga 0-2 Real Madrid |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39926301 |access-date=2026-08-12 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He added ten matches in [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League|the campaign's Champions League]], scoring once in the group stage<ref>{{Cite news |date=2016-10-18 |title=Real Madrid 5-1 Legia Warsaw |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/37671862 |access-date=2026-08-12 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> as his team also conquered the latter tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 June 2017 |title=Majestic Real Madrid win Champions League in Cardiff |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c5117c008df-de0901ea6dae-1000--majestic-real-madrid-win-champions-league-in-cardiff/ |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=UEFA.com |language=en}}</ref> 

Vázquez made ten appearances during the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|2017–18 Champions League]] and added one goal,<ref>{{Cite web |date=25 May 2018 |title=Así llegan Real Madrid y Liverpool a la final de la Champions |trans-title=That is how Real Madrid and Liverpool arrive to the Champions final |url=https://www.rcnradio.com/deportes/asi-llegan-las-plantillas-de-real-madrid-y-liverpool-la-final-de-la-champions |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=RCN Radio Newsroom |language=es}}</ref> when Real Madrid won their third consecutive and 13th overall title in the competition.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 May 2018 |title=Madrid beat Liverpool to complete hat-trick |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0245-0e98d7318379-716954065574-1000--madrid-beat-liverpool-to-complete-hat-trick/ |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=UEFA.com |language=en}}</ref> In November 2019, Vázquez broke his toe after dropping a weight on it.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2019-11-21 |title=Lucas Vazquez: Real Madrid winger 'drops weight' which breaks toe |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50507364 |access-date=2026-08-12 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> After returning, he made 18 appearances during the league season, as Real Madrid won the [[2019–20 La Liga]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Español |first=En |date=2020-07-16 |title=Real Madrid win the longest LaLiga Santander season |url=https://e01-marca.uecdn.es/en/football/real-madrid/2020/07/17/5f10db2146163f3c2c8b45d7.html |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=MARCA in English |language=en}}</ref>

[[File:Ofrenda de la Liga y la Champions-57-L.Millán (52109310843).jpg|thumb|299x299px|Vázquez with the squad presenting the [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League|Champions League trophy]] to [[Virgin of Almudena]] in 2022]]

Being a regular starter during the [[2020–21 Real Madrid CF season|2020–21 season]], Vázquez injured himself on 10 April 2021, in a 2–1 [[El Clásico]] win over [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and was ruled out for the remainder of the season with a [[Posterior cruciate ligament injury]] in his left knee.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-04-11 |title=Lucas Vazquez's season is over |url=https://e01-marca.uecdn.es/en/football/real-madrid/2021/04/11/6072e9e022601d0f0e8b45fc.html |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=MARCA |language=en}}</ref> On 3 June 2021, Vázquez signed a new three-year contract, which would keep him until 2024 at Madrid.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 June 2021 |title=Official Announcement: Lucas Vázquez |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/06/03/official-announcement-lucas-vazquez |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624211805/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/06/03/official-announcement-lucas-vazquez |archive-date=24 June 2021 |access-date=3 June 2021 |website=Real Madrid CF}}</ref> On 18 July 2024, Vázquez signed a new one-year contract, which runs until 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 July 2024 |title=Official Announcement: Lucas Vázquez |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/06/03/official-announcement-lucas-vazquez |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230416222140/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/06/03/official-announcement-lucas-vazquez |archive-date=16 April 2023 |access-date=18 July 2024 |website= |publisher=Real Madrid CF}}</ref>

On 24 May 2025, Vázquez made his 400th appearance for Real Madrid in a 2–0 win over Real Sociedad in the final match of the [[2024–25 La Liga|2024–25 season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Lucas Vázquez, 400 appearances for Real Madrid |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/lucas-vazquez-400-partidos-con-el-real-madrid-24-05-2025 |access-date=17 July 2025 |work=Real Madrid |date=24 May 2025}}</ref> On 16 July 2025, Vázquez announced that he left Real Madrid after 10 years at the club.<ref>{{cite news |title=Emotivo acto de homenaje y despedida de Lucas Vázquez |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/es-ES/noticias/futbol/primer-equipo/actualidad/emotivo-acto-de-homenaje-y-despedida-de-lucas-vazquez-17-07-2025 |access-date=17 July 2025 |work=www.realmadrid.com |date=17 July 2025 |language=es}}</ref>

===Bayer Leverkusen===
On 26 August 2025, Vázquez joined [[Bundesliga]] club [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen]] as a free agent, signing a deal valid until 2027.<ref>{{cite web |date=26 August 2025 |title=Bayer 04 sign Real legend Lucas Vázquez |url=https://www.bayer04.de/en-us/news/bayer04/bayer-04-sign-real-legend-lucas-vazquez |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250826163955/https://www.bayer04.de/en-us/news/bayer04/bayer-04-sign-real-legend-lucas-vazquez |archive-date=26 August 2025 |access-date=26 August 2025 |publisher=[[Bayer 04 Leverkusen]]}}</ref> He scored his first goal on 24 January 2026, in a 1–0 win over [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] in the [[2025–26 Bundesliga|Bundesliga]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Leverkusen 1-0 Bremen (Jan 24, 2026) Final Score |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/746883/werder-bremen-bayer-leverkusen |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=www.espn.com}}</ref>

==International career == 

Vázquez did not represent [[Spain national football team|Spain]] at any [[Spain national youth football team|youth level]]. On 17 May 2016 he, [[Saúl (footballer, born 1994)|Saúl]] and [[Sergio Rico]] were the three [[Cap (sport)|uncapped]] players named in [[Vicente del Bosque]]'s provisional squad for [[UEFA Euro 2016]] in France,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36312769|title=Euro 2016: Diego Costa, Juan Mata & Fernando Torres not in Spain squad|work=BBC Sport|date=17 May 2016|access-date=17 May 2016}}</ref> and he also made it to the final list of 23.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://deportes.elpais.com/deportes/2016/05/31/actualidad/1464710610_277737.html?rel=cx_articulo|title=Isco y Saúl fuera de la lista de Del Bosque para la Eurocopa 2016|trans-title=Isco and Saúl out of Del Bosque's list for 2016 European Championship|newspaper=[[El País]]|language=es|date=31 May 2016|access-date=3 June 2016}}</ref> 

He made his debut on 7 June, starting and playing 61 minutes in a 0–1 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] loss to [[Georgia national football team|Georgia]] at the [[Coliseum Alfonso Pérez]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/eurocopa/20160607/402350058688/derrota-preocupante-de-la-roja.html|title=Derrota preocupante de la Roja|trans-title=Worrying defeat for the ''Roja''|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es|date=7 June 2016|access-date=7 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160608134034/http://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/eurocopa/20160607/402350058688/derrota-preocupante-de-la-roja.html|archive-date=8 June 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He appeared once in the tournament, replacing [[Álvaro Morata]] in the 70th minute of a 0–2 [[Single-elimination tournament|round-of-16]] defeat against [[Italy national football team|Italy]] at the [[Stade de France]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Massimo |first=Luongo |date=2026-06-02 |title=mu88 |url=https://mu88a.jp.net |access-date=2026-08-12 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0253-0d81b24e0059-7534c6d3e771-1000--dominant-italy-brush-aside-holders-spain-in-euro-2016-first/|title=Dominant Italy brush aside champions Spain|publisher=UEFA|date=27 June 2016|access-date=27 June 2016}}</ref> 

He was then included in the final [[2018 FIFA World Cup squads|squad]] for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/morata-misses-out-on-spain-world-cup-squad/1ub1qz7jod09i1lfvdcy84ea2l|title=Morata misses out on Spain's 23-man World Cup squad|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|date=21 May 2018|access-date=21 May 2018}}</ref> making his debut in [[FIFA World Cup|the competition]] on 15 June when he replaced [[David Silva]] for the final four minutes of the 3–3 group stage draw to [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wallace |first=Sam |last2=Bagchi |first2=Rob |date=2018-06-15 |title=Cristiano Ronaldo scores sensational hat-trick as Portugal hold Spain in instant World Cup classic |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-cup/2018/06/15/portugal-vs-spain-world-cup-2018-live-score-latest-updates/ |access-date=2026-08-12 |work=The Telegraph |language=en-GB |issn=0307-1235}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Vázquez is married to Macarena Rodríguez, with whom he has three children: Lucas Jr., born in 2018, Macarena, born in 2020, and Benji, born in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |url= https://www.abc.es/estilo/gente/abci-lucas-vazquez-y-macarena-rodriguez-convierten-padres-nino-201806010908_noticia.html |title= Lucas Vázquez y Macarena Rodríguez se convierten en padres de un niño |date=1 June 2018 |access-date=3 October 2026 |newspaper=ABC |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url= https://www.hola.com/actualidad/20201221181479/lucas-vazquez-dedica-gol-hija/ |title= Lucas Vázquez dedica un gol a su hija 'mofletitos' y ella le responde así |first=Paloma |last=Anaya |date=21 December 2020 |access-date=3 October 2026 |website=¡Hola! |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url= https://www.hola.com/actualidad/20230519232256/luvas-vazquez-futbolista-presenta-tercer-hijo/ |title=Lucas Vázquez y Macarena Rodríguez presentan a su tercer hijo con la imagen más divertida de su numerosa familia |first=Belén |last=Nava M. |date=19 May 2023 |access-date=3 October 2026 |website=!Hola! |language=es}}</ref>

==Career statistics==
